name: _AnyIdentifiedView
abstract: Type-erased peek at `_IdentifiedView` so the reconciler can extract the inner content and stable id without knowing the inner type.

name: _AnyModifiedContent
abstract: Type-erased helper that lets `ViewGraph` materialise (and update) a `ModifiedContent` without knowing its generic parameters at the call site.

name: _AroundApplyingModifier
abstract: Marker for `ViewModifier`s that need to wrap descendant materialisation — installing some ambient state for the duration of the recursion and tearing it down afterwards.
discussion:
Like `_ScopeApplyingModifier`, the materialiser allocates a synthetic
anchor `Node` per slot so the modifier has a stable place to cache state
across recompose passes. The closure must be invoked exactly once — it is
what materialises (or reconciles) the wrapped content.

Routing rule: modifiers conforming to this protocol are NOT consulted via
`apply(node:)` / `apply(layout:)`. Their behaviour is delivered exclusively
through `_aroundApply(node:perform:)`.

name: _IdentifiedView
abstract: Wrapper produced by the `.id(_:)` modifier. Carries an explicit identity alongside the wrapped content.
discussion:
Reconciler behaviour (Phase 2):
- Single-root content keeps its node, stamped with `id` in `Node.key`.
  Structural content (tuples, conditionals and arrays) owns one keyed,
  layout-transparent anchor so its children reconcile as one identity.
- During reconcile, `(viewTag, key)` matches a previously identified node
  even after sibling reorder. State stored in the node's `attachments`
  and any nested user-view scopes anchored on it survive the reorder.

name: _MemoizedView
abstract: Composition's explicit reuse seam; ordinary views keep conservative input comparison.

name: _PrimitiveView
declaration: public protocol _PrimitiveView: View where Body == Never
abstract: Internal hook for views that materialise into a real `Node` (rather than expanding to other views via `body`).
discussion:
`Text` / `Image` / `Box` / `Row` / `Column` etc. (Phase 6.3) conform to this.
User-defined `View` types should never implement `_PrimitiveView` directly.

Conventions:
- `_makeNode()` creates a fresh `Node` (called once per scope per recompose).
- `_updateNode(_:)` writes view properties onto the node every materialisation.
- `_makeLayoutNode()` creates the paired `LayoutNode` (Phase 6.3+). Return
  `nil` only for views that don't participate in layout.
- `_updateLayout(_:)` writes layout-affecting properties onto the layout node.
- `_children` returns nested views to materialise as children of the produced
  node. Empty for leaf primitives.
overloads: public protocol _PrimitiveView: View where Body == Never

name: _ScopeApplyingModifier
abstract: Marker for `ViewModifier`s whose effect must be applied directly to the node produced by the wrapped content (the wrapper node), instead of being pushed down into descendant layout/render targets via `modifierTargets`.
discussion:
The canonical use is `CompositionLocal` provision: the value must live on
an ancestor of every consumer, so writing it into the wrapper node is
correct regardless of whether that node has a layout node or is a
transparent user-view anchor.

Modifiers conforming to this protocol are not consulted via
`apply(node:)` / `apply(layout:)` by the materialiser; they are routed to
`_applyScope(node:)` exclusively.

name: AccessibilityActions
abstract: Closures operate on the same controlled bindings as pointer and keyboard input.

members.name: acceptsInput
members.abstract: Whether pointer and keyboard input reach this element: every ancestor accepts subtree input and this node hit-tests. Resolved during the same walk as the snapshot, so a platform bridge does not need a second pass over the tree to answer "is this control usable".

name: AccessibilityRevision
abstract: Monotonic counters for mutations that can change the accessibility tree.
discussion:
The snapshot visits every node and the native bridge rebuilds the element
tree from it. A frame that only repaints — a spinner, a cursor blink, a
hover fade — changes nothing the walk reads, so the counters stay put and
the bridge keeps the tree it already published. It is deliberately *not*
bumped by `markRenderDirty` alone: that fires on every animated frame and
would bring the cost straight back.

Structure covers membership, semantics and input eligibility; it demands an
immediate snapshot. Geometry covers movement alone, which can be coalesced:
assistive clients poll frames, they do not need 180 updates per second.

Over-invalidating costs one rebuild; under-invalidating leaves a stale
native tree, which an assistive client reads as wrong content. Every hook
therefore sits on a mutation the walk reads, and "does this change what
VoiceOver sees?" is the test for adding another.

name: ActiveAnimationContext
abstract: Per-frame context that records the `Animation` (if any) under which the current recomposition is running, plus the completion callback waiting on it. Modifier `apply` paths read `current` when they detect that a node property is changing, and — if non-nil — register an `AnimationController` instead of writing the new value directly.
discussion:
The context is established by `withAnimation(_:_:completion:)` at the call
site of a `@State` mutation. The runtime captures this value alongside the
queued recompose body, then re-establishes it inside
`Recomposer.commitAll()` so the modifier pass observes the same animation
that the user authored.

Storage is per-thread (via `Thread.current.threadDictionary`) so that
parallel test runners — and any future multi-window UI thread — observe
independent contexts. UI work in production all runs on a single thread
so the per-thread cost is amortised.

where it is going, but an alpha, a colour channel or a corner radius

animation, on properties known to tolerate it.

name: ContainerSizeReader
abstract: Reports the content-box size of its own subtree after every layout pass, so content can adapt to the space actually available to it — a container query rather than a window query. The selected branch of a candidate layout only sees the proposal; this reader sees the measured result.
discussion:
Measurement runs after the composition that built this view, so the first
build receives `.zero` and the next frame publishes the measured size.
A size is published only when it changes by at least 0.5 points.
The reader fills its parent's available width, so changing content does
not determine the width used to select that content.

        ? AnyView(CompactCard())

}

name: HitTester
abstract: Hit-tests a `Node` tree against a window-local point.
discussion:
Algorithm:
- Frames are parent-local (set by `LayoutPass` from Yoga output).
- Points are mapped into a node's space by the *inverse* of the same
  placement the renderers use, so a scaled node is hit where it is drawn
  rather than where layout left it.
- Children are drawn in array order (last child on top → reverse iterate).
- `clipsToBounds == true` rejects child hits outside this node's frame.
- `isHitTestable == false` skips a node but keeps walking its children
  (matches CSS `pointer-events: none` semantics for the node alone).

name: RubberBand
abstract: Maps a raw overscroll past a scroll bound onto the smaller, progressively stiffening distance that is actually drawn — the rubber band.
discussion: The curve is UIKit's:

```
projected(x) = (c · |x| · d) / (d + c · |x|)
```

where `x` is signed overscroll, `d` the viewport extent along the scrolled
axis and `c` the compliance (initial slope). Three properties fall out of
this shape and are the reason it is used instead of, say, halving the
distance:
- slope at `x = 0` is exactly `c`, so the first point after the bound feels
  like the configured resistance rather than like a dead zone;
- the function is monotonically increasing, so dragging further always
  moves further — never "sticks";
- it approaches `d` asymptotically, so content can never be dragged further
  off-screen than one viewport, no matter how hard the user pushes.

members.abstract: Project `overscroll` (signed, may be negative for the leading bound) onto the visible displacement.

- Parameters:
  - overscroll: distance past the bound, in content points.
  - extent: viewport size along the same axis. Must be positive for the
    elastic response to exist; with no viewport there is nothing to
    stretch against, so the result is `0` (hard clamp).
  - compliance: initial slope, see `ScrollRubberBandSettings`.
- Returns: the displacement actually applied to the content.

members.abstract: Signed overscroll of `value` against the closed range `0...maximum`. `0` when inside the range.

members.abstract: Inverse of `project` — recovers how far input must have pushed to reach the given visible displacement.
discussion:
Needed when new input interrupts an in-flight return spring: whatever
the spring has already recovered has to be folded back into the raw
position through this inverse, otherwise the content jumps back out to
the full stretch on every new delta.

Returns `0` when the displacement is not achievable (`visibleOverscroll`
at or past the `extent` asymptote) rather than diverging.

name: ScrollMomentumSettings
abstract: Tuning for inertial scrolling — the glide that carries content along after the input that produced it has stopped.
discussion:
Applies to explicitly managed custom gestures using `ScrollAnimator`.
`idleWindow` infers release only for that API; native wheel/trackpad input
follows the platform stream directly and does not use these settings.

members.name: isEnabled
members.abstract: `false` stops content dead the moment input stops.

members.name: deceleration
members.abstract: Decay rate in nepers per second: velocity is multiplied by `e^-rate` each second. Together with `maximumVelocity` this decides how far the hardest possible throw travels — `(v₀ - restVelocity) / rate`, so `4.2` and `1100` take a full-strength flick about 261pt further, with a gradual tail reaching 2pt/s after about 1.5 seconds. iOS' `DecelerationRate.normal` (≈ e^-2.0 per second) is tuned for a finger on glass and reads as "launched" with a mouse: several viewports of travel and a tail that drifts for two seconds. Higher stops sooner.

members.name: minimumVelocity
members.abstract: Launch speed, in points per second, below which the gesture counts as placed rather than thrown and no glide starts. High enough that nudging content into place — the thing you do once it is nearly right — never sets it moving again.

members.name: restVelocity
members.abstract: Speed at which an existing glide comes to rest. Kept separate from the launch threshold: stopping at 50pt/s visibly cuts off the slow tail.

members.name: maximumVelocity
members.abstract: Ceiling on the launch speed. Wheel notches arrive milliseconds apart, so the measured slope of even a modest burst is enormous; without a ceiling one such burst throws the viewport across the whole document.

members.name: minimumSampleCount
members.abstract: Samples a gesture must have produced inside `trackingWindow` before it counts as a throw.
discussion:
A short sample pair can exaggerate velocity; require enough samples
from the custom gesture to distinguish a throw from a placement.

members.name: idleWindow
members.abstract: Quiet period, in seconds, after the newest wheel sample before the glide launches. Must outlast the gap between two notches of the same burst, or every burst turns into several glides fighting each other.

members.name: trackingWindow
members.abstract: Age limit, in seconds, of samples contributing to the launch velocity.

members.name: staleWindow
members.abstract: How long the newest sample keeps describing the gesture, in seconds.
discussion:
A drag lets go whenever the user lets go, so silence is not a signal on
its own: holding a thumb still for a while and *then* releasing must not
fling, while the wheel — whose samples always stop `idleWindow` before
the release is noticed — must. Anything quiet for this long was released
earlier. Sits comfortably clear of `idleWindow` on purpose.

discussion:
Wheel notches arrive at irregular intervals and each one travels a
different distance, so `delta / deltaTime` taken between the last two
events is unusably jittery: one notch that lands slightly late reads as
half speed, and a trackpad emits dozens of unequal deltas per second.
UIKit and Android both fit a line across a short window of samples instead.
That is what this does.
One instance per axis — a scroll container keeps two, one for each.

two events happened to be split, so merging or dropping one event does
not change the answer.

lies between the last sample and now is silence by definition, so
measuring across it would report the pause rather than the gesture.

Returns `0` when there is nothing usable to fit: a single sample
carries no direction, and a gesture that stopped moving has genuinely
come to rest.

- Parameters:

  - staleAfter: age past which the newest sample is treated as the end

property is already moving is *the same curve evaluated at a non-zero
start*, not a new curve from rest. That is the whole difference between an
interrupted animation continuing and an interrupted animation restarting —
a fixed-duration curve has no way to express it, because it only ever maps
elapsed time to progress.

Closed form rather than stepwise integration, for two reasons: the result
is independent of frame timing (a dropped frame does not change where the
spring ends up), and evaluating at absolute time makes resuming free.

members.name: addShadow
members.declaration: public func addShadow(_ layer: SurfaceShadow, rect: UIRect, cornerRadius: Float, opacity: Float = 1, frostedRect: UIRect? = nil, occludedRect: UIRect? = nil)
members.abstract: Paint one shadow layer as a stack of expanded translucent rounded rects.
discussion:
The renderer has no blurred primitive, so the gradient is built from
concentric rects: the outermost is the faint fringe, and each one on top
is smaller and denser, which accumulates into a falloff near the
surface.

`frostedRect` is the panel a backdrop blur will sample, when it has one.
The shadow is then clipped to the band outside it: a panel's own shadow
falls on what is *behind* the panel, so letting the frost sample it
greys the panel from the inside — measured at −17% luma on white.

`occludedRect` is a surface that will be painted opaquely over this node
straight after, so the shadow's interior can never be seen. Skipping it
keeps a `blur: 8` shadow from costing 33 full-surface fills, which
dominated GPU time on card-dense layouts. Corners stay rounded there;
clipping to plain bands would square the card's outline.

name: EventDispatcher
abstract: Routes window-local input events to nodes in the CoveUI tree.
discussion:
Per-window, per-tree. Construct one `EventDispatcher` for each `NodeTree`
and feed it events from `SDL3PlatformHost`'s polling loop.

Delivery model (DOM-style):
1. `capture` phase — root → target, ancestors get a chance first
2. `target` phase — the deepest hit-tested node
3. `bubble`  phase — target → root, ancestors get a chance last

A handler returning `.handled` stops propagation in the current phase.
`PointerCapture.acquire` overrides hit-testing for non-down pointer events.

name: LayerAwareNodeRenderer
abstract: Executes a flat paint plan and records each layer-root subtree into its own cached `DrawList`, then composites cached layer slices into the frame `DrawList` by appending their vertices/indices.
discussion:
Cache invariants per layer-root `RenderObject`:
- `cacheInvalid == false` AND
- the layer's placement at composite time matches the one captured when the
  cache was recorded (`lastPlacement`: position, paint and shadow scales) AND
- the layer's parent clip stack at composite time matches the one captured
  when the cache was recorded (tracked by `lastClipStack`).

Stable unclipped leaf layers may move under the same parent clip without
re-recording. Their cached vertices are translated while being appended;
this is the common path for text and controls moving during scrolling. That
shortcut needs the scale to be unchanged as well — translating vertices
cannot resize them, so a scaling layer has to re-record.

Visible geometry matches `NodeRenderer` for the same tree. Completely
clipped subtrees and cached offscreen leaves can be omitted. Cached layers
append as independent batch runs rather than coalescing across boundaries.

name: Node
abstract: A retained-mode node in the CoveUI scene tree.
discussion:
Nodes are reference types — identity is by pointer.
Dirty flags propagate upward so the root always knows when a flush is needed.

Invariant: the scene tree is owned and mutated only on the main thread (the
host run loop drives compose / layout / dispatch there). `@unchecked
Sendable` records that contract — nodes are never mutated concurrently — so
they can cross the `Sendable` boundaries the runtime API imposes without
per-field synchronisation.

members.name: id
members.abstract: Stable runtime identifier minted at construction. Phase 1: surfaced through `SceneInspector` so DevTools can correlate nodes across snapshots and invalidation events. Future phases key state, layout, render and input data off this id rather than `ObjectIdentifier`.

members.name: renderOrderedChildren
members.abstract: Children ordered for paint/hit-test, sorted by `zIndex` (stable by sibling order) when any child uses a non-zero zIndex.

members.name: isInteractionEnabled
members.abstract: Disables input for this entire subtree while retaining it for an exit transition.

members.name: subtreeOpacity
members.abstract: Alpha applied to the complete rendered subtree, including cached layers.

members.name: frame
members.abstract: The rectangle assigned by the layout engine (Phase 3). Coordinates are local to the parent node.
discussion:
Geometry single funnel (坏味 #1): `frame` and the other geometry /
hit-classification fields below (`contentOffset`, `zIndex`,
`clipsToBounds`, `isHitTestable`) all route their `didSet` through
`invalidateGeometry` — the one place that drops the hit cache. There is
no second invalidation path, so a moving property cannot be added that
silently forgets to invalidate (the "works once then stops responding
after a reflow" bug class).

members.name: isHitTestable
members.abstract: When false, hit-testing skips this node (children are still visited unless `clipsToBounds` excludes them by frame). Routes through the geometry funnel so toggling it at runtime drops the hit cache.

members.name: allowsHitTesting
members.abstract: Disable interaction for an entire subtree during a removal transition.

members.name: isFocusable
members.abstract: When true, this node may receive keyboard focus (FocusChain consideration).

members.name: automaticallyFocusOnPointerDown
members.abstract: Controls that choose focus from their own pointer geometry can disable the dispatcher's fallback focus (for example, a letterboxed viewport).

members.name: clipsToBounds
members.abstract: When true, hit-testing rejects child hits that fall outside this node's frame. Also a hint to the renderer (Phase 6.3 `.clip()` modifier).

members.name: isScrollViewport
members.abstract: A clipping node that scrolls its content, so content past its edges stays reachable. Layout diagnostics report overflow cut off by any other clipping node.

members.name: requestReveal
members.abstract: Raise or clear this node's frame-level reveal. Clearing it is what ends a run: a layer replays whatever it last recorded, so a request left behind would keep compositing after the reveal is over.

members.name: debugBackgroundColor
members.abstract: Diagnostic override. Clearing it reveals the latest authored style.

members.name: backgroundColor
members.abstract: Solid background fill. Writes update the app style beneath an override.

members.name: backgroundGradient
members.abstract: Gradient fill, drawn in place of `backgroundColor` when set.

members.name: cornerRadius
members.abstract: Corner radius (in pixels) applied to the background fill. The clip rectangle from `clipsToBounds` remains axis-aligned — child content is not rounded yet (Phase 7).

members.name: borderColor
members.abstract: Stroke colour painted as an inset border around the background fill. Rendered by `NodeRenderer` as an outer rounded rect of the border colour with the background rect inset by `borderWidth` painted on top — gives a correct rounded-rect border without needing a real stroke primitive on the GPU side.

members.name: borderWidth
members.abstract: Width of the border in pixels. `0` (default) skips border rendering even when `borderColor` is set.

members.name: backdropBlur
members.abstract: Frosted backdrop behind the background fill, in logical points. `0` (default) paints the fill over whatever is already on screen.
discussion:
This is a request: renderers with an offscreen pass blur the frame
inside the node's box and composite it before the fill, which is why
the fill above it is a translucent material rather than a solid.

members.name: shadow
members.abstract: The shadow that defines the surface: a tighter, darker layer offset below the node. Painted under the background fill.

members.name: ambientShadow
members.abstract: A wider, fainter halo under `shadow`. Empty (default) for surfaces that sit *in* the chrome; set it for surfaces that float above it, where the separation has to read before the contact shadow does.

members.name: debugForegroundColor
members.abstract: Diagnostic tint override, including inherited foreground invalidation.

members.name: foregroundColor
members.abstract: Foreground tint. Writes update the app style beneath an override.

members.name: inheritedForegroundColor
members.abstract: The nearest explicit tint, shared by text and monochrome icons.

members.name: opacity
members.abstract: Alpha multiplier in 0..1 applied to this node and its descendants.

members.name: zIndex
members.abstract: Paint/input stacking order among siblings. Higher values render later and receive hit-testing first. Equal values preserve tree order.

members.name: updateDraw
members.declaration: public func updateDraw<Identity: Equatable>(identity: Identity, _ draw: @escaping (DrawList, CGPoint) -> Void)
members.abstract: Refresh a custom painter while invalidating render caches only when its paint-affecting identity changed. The closure is still replaced on every call, so bindings/callback captures stay current without turning an otherwise stable declarative update into a full DrawList rebuild.

members.name: updateOverlayDraw

members.name: layoutDidUpdate
members.abstract: Optional hook invoked after a layout pass writes this node's frame back from the layout tree. Used by primitives that mirror layout-derived geometry into non-tree state, such as portal overlays.

members.name: contentOffset
members.abstract: Children render translated by `-contentOffset`. Used by ScrollView to scroll its content while keeping its own clip rect anchored.

members.name: transform
members.abstract: Scale applied to this node's painted subtree about `transform.anchor`. `identity` — the default — leaves everything exactly where layout put it, so this costs nothing until something animates it.
discussion:
Goes through the same funnel as `contentOffset` because it has the same
failure mode: a render cache keyed on origin and clip alone would keep
last frame's vertices when only the scale changed, and draw a stale
image without reporting anything.

members.name: cursor

members.name: viewTag
members.abstract: Identifier for the View kind that materialised this node, derived from `String(reflecting: type(of: view))`. ViewGraph uses it to decide whether a recompose can reuse this node in place (preserving any state in `attachments`) or must rebuild.

members.name: key

Survives reorder so primitives keyed by `.id` keep their attachments and child scopes when their position among siblings changes.

members.name: attachments
members.abstract: Side table for primitive-owned persistent state that must survive a recompose. Keyed by an arbitrary string chosen by the primitive. Example: `TextField` stores its `FieldState` (cursor, selection) here so editing state is not reset every time the parent recomposes.

members.name: compositionValues
members.abstract: Values pushed onto this node by `CompositionLocal` providers, keyed by the provider's identity. Lookup walks the parent chain until a value is found; absent providers fall back to `CompositionLocal.defaultValue`.

members.name: setCompositionValue

Used by the keyed reconciler to apply a new sibling order after `addChild` / `tearDown` have already settled membership.

Ancestors are flagged so the tree root knows a flush is needed

members.abstract: Window-space origin of this node: its local frame composed down the chain, with every ancestor's scroll offset applied to its content (see `Node.placementStep(scrolling:)`) and every ancestor's `transform` applied about its own anchor.

This is THE walk for converting a node into window coordinates — any

scrolled controls at their unscrolled position (the "dead dropdown
after scrolling" bug class). It is the one walk that also accounts for
scale, so a scaled node answers here the way it is drawn.

a caller can hit-test and a platform can hand to accessibility. A
uniform scale composed with translations keeps the result axis-aligned.

name: ScrollAnimator
abstract: Owns every kind of motion one scrollable offset can have: the inertia that carries content along after input stops, the rubber band it stretches against past its bounds, and the spring that brings it back.
discussion:
Components that scroll keep one instance alongside their own state and
route every offset change through it:

Two coordinate systems are kept apart on purpose:
- **raw position** — where input has pushed the content. Unbounded input
  pushes it past `0...maximumOffset`.
- **visible offset** — what gets written out. Equal to the raw position
  inside the range, and a compressed version of it past the range.

Keeping the raw position lets a gesture continue to move the viewport even
while it is fully stretched: each new delta is added to where the user is
actually pointing, instead of to an already-clamped value that has lost the
overflow. It also gives the glide somewhere to run: coasting down a long
document must not slow down just because the visible offset is compressed
near an edge.

Each axis runs input, glide, then its own return spring —
and each one hands its leftover velocity to the next, which is what makes a
throw into the end of a list bounce instead of stopping.

While anything is moving the animator registers itself with
`AnimatorScheduler.current` so the host keeps producing frames, and drops
out again once it comes to rest.

members.name: physics
members.abstract: Behaviour tuning. May be replaced between interactions; changes take effect on the next input or settle.

members.name: onChange
members.abstract: Called whenever the visible offset changes — including once per frame while gliding or settling. The owner writes the value to wherever it keeps its scroll offset (`Node.contentOffset` for `ScrollView`).

members.name: velocity
members.abstract: Velocity of the current glide, in points per second. Zero unless coasting.

members.name: clock
members.abstract: Monotonic seconds. Replaceable so tests can drive time instead of waiting for it; nothing else should need to touch it.

members.name: isSettling
members.abstract: `true` while the return spring owns `offset`.

members.name: isGliding
members.abstract: `true` while inertia owns `offset`.

members.name: isOverscrolled
members.abstract: `true` while any axis is past its bound, regardless of whether the return spring has started.

members.name: update
members.declaration: public func update(maximumOffset: CGPoint, viewportSize: CGSize)
members.abstract: Publish freshly laid-out geometry. Cheap — call before every interaction so late-measured content still produces correct bounds.
discussion:
A range that *shrank* pulls the offset back in immediately and drops the
recorded velocity: the content the glide was aimed at may no longer be
there, so coasting into the new bounds from stale samples would be a
guess (cleared console, filtered list). Growth is left alone, otherwise
this would eat every in-flight motion.

members.name: adopt
members.abstract: Adopt an offset written by someone else — a two-way `scrollOffset:` binding, a `scrollTo` call, a layout correction.
discussion:
Interrupting motion this way is deliberate: an authoritative write wins
over an animation that is only cleaning up after a gesture.

members.name: scrollDirectly
members.declaration: public func scrollDirectly(by delta: CGPoint) -> CGPoint
members.abstract: Follow a platform-owned wheel/trackpad stream exactly. Its packets already include acceleration and OS momentum. Never arm a quiet-window fling or insert a spring between packets, including phase-only packets.

members.name: scroll
members.declaration: public func scroll(by delta: CGPoint) -> CGPoint
members.abstract: Apply one increment from an application-owned gesture and return its visible offset. With momentum enabled, silence for `idleWindow` infers release. Do not use this method for platform wheel/trackpad packets; use `scrollDirectly(by:)` to avoid adding inertia to OS momentum.
discussion:
Landing past a bound skips all of that and starts the return spring
right away, so a single notch at the end of a list produces a short pull
that relaxes back instead of a glide with nowhere to go. Further
increments re-enter through `synchronizeRawPosition`, which folds
whatever the spring has already recovered back into the raw position,
so rapid notches build up smoothly.

members.name: move
members.declaration: public func move(to newPosition: CGPoint) -> CGPoint
members.abstract: Place an application-owned gesture's raw position while recording velocity for `settle()`. A scrollbar thumb instead uses direct, clamped placement, without recording a throw.

members.name: settle
members.abstract: Release input that has stopped, whether or not anything announced it.
discussion:
Content keeps coasting when it was moving fast enough; anything leaning
past a bound springs straight back, carrying whatever speed was left
into the bounce.

Called by the custom gesture owner, or after `scroll(by:)` has been
quiet for `momentum.idleWindow`. Platform wheel and scrollbar thumb
handlers do not launch this physics path.

members.name: stopCoasting
members.abstract: Stop a glide dead where it is, leaving the current offset alone.
discussion:
Touching content that is still moving is how a user says "here", so the
pointer going down anywhere inside the container counts. The return
spring is deliberately left running: it already knows where it is
going, and stopping it would strand the content out of bounds.

members.name: finishImmediately
members.abstract: Land immediately on the in-bounds position.

members.abstract: Move to an application-owned offset over a fixed duration. This is the timed programmatic path; wheel, pointer and gesture input cancel it.

members.name: cancel

name: ViewGraph
abstract: Materialises `View` trees into the underlying `NodeTree`, and recomposes affected subtrees when `@State` writes invalidate them through `Recomposer`.
discussion:
Lifecycle:
1. `install(root:)` builds the initial tree and wires state observers.
2. State write → `Recomposer.invalidate(scopeID:body:)` queues the scope.
3. `recomposer.commitAll()` (driven by the platform host each frame) re-runs
   each queued scope's body and reconciles the produced views against the
   existing nodes in place.

Components and primitives share retained composition scopes. The transaction
executor evaluates a flat work list, then publishes layout order and inherited
modifiers before the host proceeds to layout, accessibility and rendering.
